question: The base of a triangle is increased by 40%. By what percentage (correct to two decimal places) should its height be increased so that the area increases by 60%?

**Given:**

The base of a triangle is increased by 40%

The area of a triangle is increased by 60%

**Formula used:**

Area of a triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height

**Calculation:**

Let, the base of old triangle = b; the base of new triangle = b × (140/100) = 7b/5

The height of the old triangle = h; the height of the new triangle = h₁

So, (frac{1)/(2)×(7b)/(5)× h₁}{(1)/(2)× b× h}=(160)/(100)

⇒ (7/5)h₁/h = 8/5

⇒ 7h₁ = 8h

⇒ h₁/h = 8/7

The height increases = [(8 - 7)/7] × 100

= (1/7) × 100

= 14.285...%

≈ 14.29% (correct to two decimal places)

**∴ The height of the triangle should be increased by 14.29%**
